input:
Two cards are drawn successively with replacement from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Then the probability distribution of number of jacks is 

Options:
A. 
| X = x | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| P(X = x) | 144/169 | 24/169 | 1/169 |

B.
| X = x | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| P(X = x) | 1/169 | 144/169 | 24/169 |

C.
| X = x | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| P(X = x) | 24/169 | 1/169 | 144/169 |

D.
| X = x | 0 | 1 | 2 |
| P(X = x) | 144/169 | 1/169 | 24/169 |

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Create the probability distribution table for the number of jacks obtained when drawing two cards from a standard deck with replacement.

key_concepts: Binomial Distribution (since it is with replacement)

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Define the probability of success (drawing a jack) and failure, then apply the binomial probability formula for each possible value of X (0, 1, 2).
logical_steps: Step 1: Determine p (probability of jack) and q (probability of non-jack).
Step 5: Compare results with the given tables.

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: The sum of probabilities $144/169 + 24/169 + 1/169 = 169/169 = 1$. This confirms the distribution is valid. Table A contains these exact values in order.
